parts.title: 大問1 短文の語句空所補充
parts.desc: 短い文や会話の空所に入る単語・熟語・文法を4つから選ぶ
parts.tip: 空所の前後で品詞と形（後ろに前置詞や that 節を取れるか）を先に絞る。次に2文目やBの返事から理由・結果のヒントを探す。熟語は動詞と前置詞のセットで覚えておく。
parts.intro: Choose the word or phrase that best fills the blank in each item.

questions.q: The museum guide spoke so ____ that even the people standing at the back of the large group could hear every word.
questions.why: spoke so clearly that ～＝「とてもはっきり話したので～」。後ろの人まで全部聞こえた、という結果と合う。rarely（めったに～ない）、slightly（わずかに）、barely（かろうじて）では聞こえた理由にならない。

questions.q:
A: Did you enjoy the concert last night, Sam?
B: The music was great, but the ____ was noisy. Some people kept talking during the quiet songs.
questions.why: audience＝「観客・聴衆」。コンサートで話し続けた人々を指す語。patient（患者）、author（作者）、pilot（操縦士）は場面に合わない。

questions.q: Emma had to ____ her trip to Canada because her passport did not arrive in time. She hopes to go next spring instead.
questions.why: postpone＝「延期する」。パスポートが間に合わず、来春に行く予定、という2文目から延期と分かる。repair（修理する）、deliver（配達する）、attract（引きつける）は旅行に合わない。

questions.q: The most popular ____ of the new smartphone is its battery, which can be fully charged in only ten minutes.
questions.why: feature＝「特徴・機能」。10分で充電できるバッテリーはスマホの機能。ceremony（式典）、shortage（不足）、instinct（本能）は合わない。

questions.q: Kevin was ____ to hear that he had won first prize in the photo contest. He had not expected to win anything at all.
questions.why: be amazed to ～＝「～して驚く」。何も取れないと思っていたのに1位、という流れ。annoyed（いらいらした）、bored（退屈した）、ashamed（恥じた）は1位の知らせに合わない。

questions.q: Our town's library has a large ____ of old maps. Some of them were drawn by hand more than 200 years ago.
questions.why: a collection of ～＝「～の収集品・コレクション」。図書館が古い地図をたくさん持っている。reaction（反応）、direction（方向）、connection（つながり）は合わない。

questions.q: Before the test, Ms. Clark reminded her students to read each question ____ so that they would not make careless mistakes.
questions.why: うっかりミスをしないように読む＝carefully（注意深く）。loudly（大声で）、briefly（手短に）、rapidly（急いで）では、ミスを防ぐ理由にならない。

questions.q:
A: Why are you wearing such heavy boots for the hike?
B: The mountain path is rocky and ____ after it rains, and I don't want to slip and fall.
questions.why: slippery＝「すべりやすい」。後ろの I don't want to slip（すべりたくない）がヒント。generous（気前のよい）、curious（好奇心のある）、delicious（おいしい）は道の説明にならない。

questions.q: The scientists hope that their ____ of the deep ocean will help them discover new kinds of fish that nobody has ever seen before.
questions.why: exploration＝「探検・調査」。深海を調べて新しい魚を見つける話。decoration（飾り）、invitation（招待）、population（人口）は深海と結びつかない。

questions.q: Jake's grandfather is 85 years old, but he is still very ____. He walks for an hour every morning and works in his garden.
questions.why: active＝「活動的な」。85歳でも毎朝1時間歩き、庭仕事をする、という2文目が根拠。nervous（不安な）、honest（正直な）、similar（似ている）は2文目の説明にならない。

questions.q: The hotel ____ its guests a free breakfast if they stay for more than three nights, so many families choose to stay there for a week.
questions.why: offer 人 物＝「人に物を提供する」。目的語を2つ並べられるのは offer。invite は invite 人 to ～ の形になる。borrow（借りる）、accept（受け取る）はホテル側の行動として逆。

questions.q: After a long day of meetings and phone calls, Rina felt completely ____, so she went to bed as soon as she got home.
questions.why: exhausted＝「疲れ果てた」。会議と電話の長い1日のあと、すぐ寝た、という流れ。curious（好奇心のある）、delighted（喜んだ）、ordinary（普通の）ではすぐ寝る理由にならない。

questions.q:
A: Have you decided which university to apply to?
B: Not yet. I'm still trying to ____ the costs and the courses of three different schools.
questions.why: compare＝「比べる」。3つの大学の費用と授業を比べて、まだ決めていない。prevent（防ぐ）、injure（けがをさせる）、pretend（ふりをする）は大学選びに合わない。

questions.q: The bakery became famous for its bread, so the owner decided to ____ her business and open a second shop in the next town.
questions.why: expand＝「拡大する」。2号店を開く、という後半と合う。reduce（縮小する）は逆。borrow（借りる）、repeat（繰り返す）は business と組まない。

questions.q: Many tourists visit the island every summer. Its long, ____ beaches and clear blue water make it a popular place for swimming.
questions.why: sandy beaches＝「砂浜」。泳ぐのに人気の島の説明。fluent（流ちょうな）、rapid（速い）、polite（礼儀正しい）は beach を説明しない。

questions.q: Lucy's teacher says she is the most ____ actor in the drama club because she has performed in many shows since she was a child.
questions.why: experienced＝「経験豊富な」。子どもの頃から多くの舞台に出ている、という because 以下が根拠。temporary（一時的な）、modest（控えめな）、empty（空の）は理由と合わない。

questions.q: The price of vegetables has ____ a lot this year because of the hot, dry summer. Tomatoes now cost almost twice as much as last year.
questions.why: increase＝「上がる」。トマトが去年の約2倍、という2文目から値上がり。recovered（回復した）は元に戻る意味で「2倍」と合わない。disappeared・admitted も合わない。

questions.q:
A: Mom, can I have a dog?
B: Having a pet is a big ____, Ben. You'll have to walk it and feed it every day, even when you're busy.
questions.why: responsibility＝「責任」。毎日散歩させ、えさをやらなければならない、という続きが責任の中身。opportunity（機会）、tradition（伝統）、emergency（緊急事態）は続きと合わない。

questions.q: The factory has started using solar panels to ____ the amount of electricity that it buys from the power company each month.
questions.why: lower＝「下げる・減らす」。太陽光パネルで、買う電気の量を減らす。invent（発明する）、blame（責める）、announce（発表する）は the amount と組まない。

questions.q: Mr. Davis is a very ____ boss. He always listens to his workers' ideas and thanks them for their hard work.
questions.why: considerate＝「思いやりのある」。部下の考えを聞き、感謝する、という2文目が根拠。jealous（嫉妬深い）、stubborn（頑固な）、careless（不注意な）は2文目と逆。

questions.q: The new bicycle path is ____ from the road by a row of trees, so riders do not have to worry about cars.
questions.why: be separated from ～＝「～から分けられている」。木の列で道路と分かれているので、車を気にしなくてよい。combined（結合された）は逆。supported・translated は合わない。

questions.q: Ayumi's parents finally gave her ____ to study abroad for a year. She will leave for Australia in September.
questions.why: give 人 permission to ～＝「人に～する許可を与える」。9月にオーストラリアへ行く、という2文目と合う。attention（注意）、ambition（野心）、tension（緊張）は give ～ to study の形にならない。

questions.q: The soccer coach told his players that winning was not everything. He said that it was more important to show ____ for the other team.
questions.why: show respect for ～＝「～に敬意を示す」。勝つことがすべてではない、という流れ。complaint（不満）、damage（損害）、profit（利益）は合わない。

questions.q:
A: Why did you leave the party so early?
B: The music was so loud that I got a terrible headache. I couldn't ____ it any longer.
questions.why: can't stand ～＝「～に耐えられない」。頭痛がするほど音楽がうるさかった。afford（～する余裕がある）、solve（解決する）、recognize（見分ける）は合わない。

questions.q: Mark has been studying hard for the exam. His teacher told him that if he ____ up the good work, he will get a high score.
questions.why: keep up the good work＝「その調子で頑張り続ける」。give up（あきらめる）は逆。take up（始める）、bring up（育てる・話題に出す）は合わない。

questions.q: Mina was so nervous before her speech that she could not ____ down. Her friend told her to take a few deep breaths.
questions.why: calm down＝「落ち着く」。深呼吸を勧められた、という2文目と合う。break down（故障する・泣き崩れる）、hand down（伝える）、pass down（受け継ぐ）は合わない。

questions.q: The outdoor concert was ____ off because of the strong wind. The organizers said that everyone would get their money back.
questions.why: call off＝「中止する」。お金が返ってくる、という2文目と合う。turn off（消す）、take off（離陸する・脱ぐ）、keep off（近づかない）は合わない。

questions.q: Brian really ____ his father. They both have curly hair, and they both love telling jokes at family dinners.
questions.why: take after＝「（親に）似ている」。髪も冗談好きも同じ、という2文目が根拠。get over（克服する）、look into（調べる）、run out of（使い切る）は合わない。

questions.q:
A: Do you still have that old bicycle?
B: No, I ____ rid of it last year. It was too small for me, so I bought a new one.
questions.why: get rid of ～＝「～を処分する」。新しいのを買った、という流れ。make / take / keep は rid of と組まない。

questions.q: When Sophie moved to a new school, she found it hard to ____ in with her classmates at first, but now she has many close friends.
questions.why: fit in with ～＝「～になじむ」。最初は難しかったが今は友達が多い。give in（降参する）、drop in（立ち寄る）、hand in（提出する）は with classmates と合わない。

questions.q: The teacher asked the students to ____ in their essays by Friday so that she could read them over the weekend.
questions.why: hand in＝「提出する」。先生が週末に読むため、金曜までに出す。check in（宿泊の手続きをする）、fill in（記入する）、look in（のぞく）は essays と合わない。

questions.q: Mr. Tanaka is ____ charge of the new project, so if you have any questions about it, please ask him directly.
questions.why: be in charge of ～＝「～を担当している」。だから質問は彼に、という流れ。on / at / by は charge of の前に置かない。

questions.q: Nancy had a bad cold last week, but she has ____ over it now and is back at work this morning.
questions.why: get over ～＝「（病気など）から回復する」。仕事に戻った、という後半と合う。turn over（ひっくり返す）、look over（目を通す）、take over（引き継ぐ）は合わない。

questions.q: The two brothers often argue about small things, but ____ the whole, they get along well and enjoy spending time together.
questions.why: on the whole＝「全体として・概して」。よくけんかするが、全体としては仲が良い。in / by / at は the whole と組んでこの意味にならない。

questions.q: If I ____ more free time, I would join the volunteer club. But I have to work at a part-time job after school every day.
questions.why: 仮定法過去：If + 過去形, would + 動詞の原形。実際は時間が無いので had。have / will have / have had は would と組まない。

questions.q: The old stone bridge ____ in 1920 is still used by thousands of people every day, and it has become a symbol of the town.
questions.why: 「1920年に建てられた橋」＝過去分詞 built が後ろから bridge を説明する。橋は「建てられる」側なので building（建てている）は誤り。

questions.q: Lisa has lived in Osaka ____ she was ten years old, so she knows many good places to eat in the city.
questions.why: 現在完了 has lived + since ～＝「～以来ずっと住んでいる」。until は「～まで」で現在完了と合わない。during は後ろに文を取れない。

questions.q:
A: Is this the restaurant ____ you had your birthday party last year?
B: Yes, it is. Their pasta is really delicious, so I come here often.
questions.why: 後ろが you had your party と欠けの無い文なので、場所を表す関係副詞 where。which を使うなら at which が必要。

questions.q: Daniel was so busy with his homework that he forgot ____ his grandmother back. He called her the next morning to say sorry.
questions.why: forget to ～＝「（これから）～するのを忘れる」。電話をしなかったので to call。forget ～ing は「～したことを忘れる」で、実際に電話したことになる。

questions.q: ____ by many young people around the world, the new language-learning app has become one of the most popular apps of the year.
questions.why: 分詞構文。アプリは「使われる」側なので過去分詞 Used（＝Because it is used）。Using だとアプリが使う意味になる。

questions.q:
A: Should I take an umbrella to the game tonight?
B: Yes. The weather report said there was a 70 percent ____ of rain this evening.
questions.why: a 70 percent chance of rain＝「降水確率70％」。chance of ～で「～の可能性」。reason（理由）、habit（習慣）、matter（問題）は of rain と組んで確率を表さない。

questions.q: The company plans to ____ the old factory into a shopping center with restaurants and a movie theater.
questions.why: convert A into B＝「AをBに変える・改造する」。工場をショッピングセンターに変える。persuade（説得する）、approve（承認する）、inspect（検査する）は into B の形を取らない。

questions.q: Tim's ____ is to become a doctor who works in poor areas around the world. He studies biology every night to make his dream come true.
questions.why: goal＝「目標」。2文目の make his dream come true（夢をかなえる）と合う。hobby（趣味）、mistake（間違い）、rumor（うわさ）では夢の話にならない。

questions.q: Ms. Hayes always ____ her students to ask questions whenever they did not understand something. She said that there were no bad questions.
questions.why: encourage 人 to ～＝「人に～するよう勧める・励ます」。「悪い質問は無い」と言っているので質問を勧めている。refuse は refuse 人 to ～ の形を取らない。ignored（無視した）、bothered（困らせた）は2文目と合わない。

questions.q: The road along the river was ____ for three hours after a large tree fell across it during the storm.
questions.why: be blocked＝「ふさがれる・通れなくなる」。大きな木が倒れて道をふさいだ。painted（塗られた）、folded（折りたたまれた）、printed（印刷された）は倒木と結びつかない。

questions.q: Before you sign up for the course, please read the information carefully and make sure that all the ____, such as the dates and the price, are correct.
questions.why: details＝「細かい点・詳細」。such as the dates and the price（日付や値段など）が具体例。habits（習慣）、shadows（影）、riddles（なぞなぞ）は日付や値段の言い換えにならない。

questions.q: Sarah's new job is very ____. She has to answer phone calls, write reports, and meet customers, often all on the same day.
questions.why: demanding＝「（仕事などが）大変な・きつい」。電話・報告書・客との面会を同じ日にこなす、という2文目が根拠。peaceful（穏やかな）は逆。accidental（偶然の）、fragile（壊れやすい）は仕事の説明にならない。

questions.q: The children were ____ by the magician's tricks. They could not believe that he made a rabbit appear from an empty hat.
questions.why: be fascinated by ～＝「～に魅了される」。空の帽子からウサギ、という驚きの場面。punished（罰せられた）、employed（雇われた）、rescued（救助された）は手品を見た子どもの様子に合わない。

questions.q: The city library ____ students to borrow up to ten books at a time, so many of them visit it before their summer vacation.
questions.why: allow 人 to ～＝「人が～するのを許す」。一度に10冊まで借りられる。suggest / insist / demand は「人 to ～」の形を取らない。

questions.q: The doctor told Mr. Lee that his illness was not serious and that he would make a full ____ in a few weeks.
questions.why: make a full recovery＝「完全に回復する」。病気が重くない、という流れ。discovery（発見）、delivery（配達）、victory（勝利）はつづりが似ているだけで意味が合わない。

questions.q: The hikers had to ____ the river very carefully because the water was deep and moving fast.
questions.why: cross the river＝「川を渡る」。深くて流れが速いので注意して渡る。chase（追いかける）、swallow（飲み込む）、wrap（包む）は川と組まない。

questions.q: This T-shirt is made of ____ cotton, so it feels soft and does not contain any plastic.
questions.why: pure cotton＝「綿100％」。プラスチック（化学繊維）を含まない、という後半と合う。brave（勇敢な）、rude（失礼な）、eager（熱心な）は人の性質で、素材を説明しない。

questions.q:
A: Which puppy are you going to take home, Mia?
B: I can't ____ between them. They are both so cute!
questions.why: choose between A and B＝「AとBのどちらかを選ぶ」。どちらもかわいくて選べない。suffer（苦しむ）、wander（歩き回る）、bother（悩ませる）は between them と組んで「選ぶ」の意味にならない。

questions.q: Our school has a strict ____ about smartphones. Students must turn them off and keep them in their lockers during classes.
questions.why: policy＝「方針・規則」。授業中は電源を切ってロッカーに、という2文目が規則の中身。climate（気候）、region（地域）、rhythm（リズム）は合わない。

questions.q: Jun's parents were very ____ of him when he passed the entrance exam for the university he had always wanted to go to.
questions.why: be proud of ～＝「～を誇りに思う」。志望大学に合格した息子に対する気持ち。scared of（～を怖がる）、sick of（～にうんざりする）、careful of（～に気をつける）は合格の場面に合わない。

questions.q: The new train line will ____ the time it takes to travel from the airport to the city center by about 20 minutes.
questions.why: shorten＝「短くする」。新路線で空港から都心までの時間が約20分短くなる。widen（広げる）、soften（柔らかくする）、deepen（深める）は時間と組まない。

questions.q: The weather in the mountains is ____. It can be sunny in the morning and then suddenly start snowing in the afternoon.
questions.why: unpredictable＝「予測できない」。朝は晴れでも午後に急に雪、という2文目が根拠。unavoidable（避けられない）、unemployed（失業した）、unfriendly（不親切な）は天気の説明に合わない。

questions.q: Paul ____ for being late to the meeting. He explained that his train had stopped for twenty minutes because of a signal problem.
questions.why: apologize for ～＝「～のことで謝る」。遅刻の理由を説明している。suffer from（苦しむ）、argue（言い争う）、admire（感心する）は for being late と合わない。

questions.q: The new shopping mall is expected to ____ more than 500 jobs for people who live in the area.
questions.why: create jobs＝「仕事（雇用）を生み出す」。新しいモールで500人以上の働き口ができる。waste（むだにする）、borrow（借りる）、hide（隠す）は合わない。

questions.q:
A: This soup tastes a little ____.
B: Oh, sorry. I think I forgot to add salt. Let me get some for you.
questions.why: plain＝「（味が）薄い・あっさりした」。塩を入れ忘れた、という返事が根拠。salty（塩辛い）は逆。crowded（混んだ）、polished（磨かれた）は味の説明にならない。

questions.q: Jenna's apartment is in a very ____ location. It is only a two-minute walk to the station, and there is a supermarket next door.
questions.why: convenient＝「便利な」。駅まで徒歩2分、隣にスーパー、という2文目が根拠。ancient（古代の）、anxious（不安な）、annual（年1回の）は場所の便利さを表さない。

questions.q: The scientist spent ten years doing experiments to ____ her idea that some plants can grow faster when they hear music.
questions.why: prove＝「証明する」。10年実験して自分の考えを証明しようとした。greet（あいさつする）、hire（雇う）、bake（焼く）は idea と組まない。

questions.q: While Ken was cleaning his grandfather's house, he ____ across some old photos of his family from the 1960s.
questions.why: come across ～＝「～を偶然見つける」。掃除中に古い写真を見つけた。take / give / put は across と組んでこの意味にならない。

questions.q: Because of the heavy rain, the school decided to ____ off the sports day until next Saturday.
questions.why: put off＝「延期する」。until next Saturday（来週の土曜まで）と合う。turn off（消す）、show off（見せびらかす）、pass off（偽って通す）は行事と合わない。

questions.q: Only five members ____ up for the club meeting because of the snowstorm, so the leader decided to have it again next week.
questions.why: show up＝「（会などに）来る・現れる」。吹雪で5人しか来なかった。hold up（遅らせる）、break up（解散する・別れる）、fill up（満たす）は合わない。

questions.q: Lily ____ down the job offer because the office was too far from her home. She wants to find a job closer to where she lives.
questions.why: turn down＝「断る」。遠すぎるので仕事の申し出を断った。look down（見下ろす）、sit down（座る）、write down（書き留める）は job offer と合わない。

questions.q: Many young players ____ up to the team captain because he always practices the hardest and helps others.
questions.why: look up to ～＝「～を尊敬する」。一番練習し人を助けるキャプテン。set up（準備する）、break up（解散する）、end up（結局～になる）は to the captain と合わない。

questions.q: Jim was sick for a week, so he worked on Saturday to ____ up for the time he had lost.
questions.why: make up for ～＝「～の埋め合わせをする」。休んだ分を土曜に働いて取り戻す。take up（始める）、pick up（拾う）、turn up（現れる）は for the time と組まない。

questions.q: Tom could not ____ out how to use the new coffee machine, so he read the instructions again.
questions.why: figure out＝「理解する・分かる」。使い方が分からず説明書を読み直した。drop out（脱落する）、hang out（ぶらぶらする）、pass out（気を失う）は how to ～ を目的語に取らない。

questions.q: The students will ____ out a survey about how much time people in their town spend on their phones each day.
questions.why: carry out＝「実行する・行う」。carry out a survey＝「調査を行う」。wear out（すり減らす）、fall out（抜け落ちる・仲たがいする）、sell out（売り切る）は survey と組まない。

questions.q: If you want to eat at that popular restaurant on a weekend, you need to make a reservation at least a week ____ advance.
questions.why: in advance＝「前もって」。人気店なので1週間前に予約する。on / at / for は advance と組んでこの意味にならない。

questions.q: Yuta deleted an important file ____ mistake, but luckily his teacher still had a copy of it.
questions.why: by mistake＝「間違って・うっかり」。幸い先生がコピーを持っていた、という流れ。with / in / at は mistake と組んでこの意味にならない。

questions.q: While Mr. and Mrs. Brown are on vacation, their neighbor will ____ after their cat and water their plants.
questions.why: look after ～＝「～の世話をする」。留守中に猫の世話と水やり。take after（～に似ている）、run after / go after（～を追いかける）は意味が合わない。

questions.q: I wish I ____ how to swim. Then I could go to the beach with my friends this summer.
questions.why: I wish + 過去形＝「～ならいいのに」（今の事実と違う願い）。実際は泳げない。know / will know / have known は wish の後ろで今の願いを表せない。

questions.q: The man ____ car broke down on the highway called a repair company for help.
questions.why: 後ろが car broke down と名詞から始まり「その人の車」なので所有格の関係代名詞 whose。who / which / whom の後ろに car は続かない。

questions.q: By the time we arrived at the theater, the movie ____ already started, so we missed the first ten minutes.
questions.why: By the time + 過去の文 → それより前に完了した事は過去完了 had started。has / have は現在完了、is は現在形で、過去の時点（arrived）より前を表せない。

questions.q: Ms. Kato made her son ____ his room before he went out to play with his friends.
questions.why: make 人 ＋動詞の原形＝「人に～させる」。to clean は make の後ろには来ない（受け身の時だけ to が付く）。

questions.q: It was ____ a hot day that we decided to stay inside and watch movies instead of going to the park.
questions.why: such a ＋形容詞＋名詞 that ～＝「とても…なので～」。後ろに a hot day（名詞）があるので such。so なら so hot a day の語順になる。

questions.q: If it ____ tomorrow, the baseball game will be canceled, and the players will practice in the gym.
questions.why: 条件を表す if 節の中では、未来のことでも現在形 rains を使う。主節が will be なので仮定法の rained / would rain は合わない。

questions.q: Mark is used to ____ up early because he has worked at a bakery for many years.
questions.why: be used to ～ing＝「～するのに慣れている」。この to は前置詞なので後ろは動名詞 getting。used to get（以前はよく起きた）と混同しないこと。

parts.title: 大問2 長文の語句空所補充
parts.desc: 約245語の説明文（3段落）の空所3つに入る語句を選ぶ
parts.tip: 空所のすぐ後ろの1〜2文が根拠になることが多い。つなぎ語の空所は、前後が「逆」「追加」「結果」「例」のどれかを先に決めてから選択肢を見る。
parts.intro: Read the passage and choose the best word or phrase for each numbered blank.

sets.passage:
Phone-Free Concerts

At many concerts today, people in the audience hold up their smartphones to take videos of the show. Some musicians, however, have started asking fans to ( 1 ). At the entrance, each person's phone is put into a small cloth bag that locks. Fans keep the bag with them, but they cannot open it until they leave the concert hall. If someone needs to make an emergency call, they can go to a special area outside where staff will unlock the bag.

Many fans were unhappy about this rule at first. They wanted to share videos with their friends online. After the concerts, though, a large number of them said that they ( 2 ). Without their phones, they were able to focus on the music, and they did not have to look at a sea of bright screens in front of them. Some fans even said that they could remember the songs better because they had watched with their own eyes.

The musicians also see benefits. They say that they can see people's faces and feel the energy of the crowd. Some also worry that videos taken during a concert may spread online before a new song is officially released. ( 3 ), not everyone is in favor of the idea. Parents who want to stay in touch with their children may feel uneasy, and some fans think that a ticket holder should be free to decide how to enjoy the show.

choices: leave their phones untouched during shows
bring two phones to the hall
buy new phones at the entrance
questions.why: 続く文で、入口でスマホを鍵付きの袋に入れ、出るまで開けられない、と説明している。つまり公演中はスマホを使わせない。写真を増やす・2台持つ・買う話は無い。

choices: would never go to a concert again
enjoyed the experience more than they expected
questions.why: 最初は不満だったが（though）、後で「音楽に集中できた」「歌をよく覚えていた」と良い感想が続く。だから「思ったより楽しめた」。返金・二度と行かない・紛失は流れと逆。
前の段落は音楽家にとっての利点。後ろは「全員が賛成ではない」と反対の声。利点を認めたうえで反論を出すので Even so（それでも）。As a result（その結果）や For example（例えば）ではつながらない。

sets.passage:
The Seed Library of Millford

When Grace Holt retired from her job as a science teacher in the small town of Millford, she wanted to do something useful for her neighbors. She had grown vegetables in her garden for many years and always had more seeds than she could use. One day, she came up with the idea of ( 1 ). She placed an old wooden cabinet in the corner of the town library and filled its drawers with small paper envelopes of seeds.

The system is simple. Anyone with a library card can take up to five envelopes of seeds for free. At the end of the growing season, people are asked to collect seeds from the best plants in their gardens and bring some back to the cabinet. In this way, ( 2 ). Over the years, the seeds in the cabinet have become well suited to Millford's cool summers and rocky soil, so they grow better there than seeds bought from stores.

Today, the seed library has more than 300 members, and Holt holds free gardening classes every spring. ( 3 ), young families who have never grown anything before can learn how to plant tomatoes and beans with their children. Holt says that the project has also brought people together. Neighbors who used to just say hello now exchange advice and share their vegetables. Other towns nearby are now planning to open seed libraries of their own.

questions.why: 続く文で、図書館に棚を置き種の封筒を入れた、とある。次の段落で「図書館カードで無料で持ち帰れる」と説明が続くので、種を貸し出すこと。野菜の販売・本・学校の話ではない。

choices: the collection keeps growing every year
the library has to buy new seeds
only teachers can use the cabinet
members must pay a small fee
questions.why: 育てた後に良い株の種を集めて戻す仕組みなので、種は毎年増えていく。続く文の「何年もかけて土地に合った種になった」とも合う。無料なので料金の話は誤り。
前の文で「毎春の無料教室」、後ろで「初心者の家族も育て方を学べる」。教室のおかげで学べる、という因果なので Thanks to。Despite（～にもかかわらず）は逆の関係。

sets.passage:
Sleeping with Half a Brain

For humans, sleep means closing our eyes and becoming unaware of the world around us for several hours. However, some animals cannot safely do this. Dolphins, for example, live in the ocean but need to come up to the surface to breathe. If they fell completely asleep, they might ( 1 ). Scientists have found that dolphins solve this problem in an interesting way. They let only one half of the brain sleep at a time, while the other half stays awake.

Some birds have the same ability. Researchers who studied a group of ducks noticed something unusual. The ducks slept in a line, and the birds at each end of the line ( 2 ). They kept the eye that faced away from the group open. That eye was connected to the half of the brain that was still awake, so the ducks could watch for danger. The ducks in the middle of the line, which were safer, usually closed both eyes.

Scientists believe that humans also do something similar, though in a much weaker way. In one study, people slept in a laboratory for two nights. On the first night, one half of their brain stayed more alert than the other. ( 3 ), this difference almost disappeared on the second night. The researchers think this explains why many people do not sleep well on their first night in a hotel or a friend's house. Part of the brain stays on guard in a new place.

questions.why: 直前で「呼吸のために水面に上がる必要がある」とある。完全に眠ると呼吸できなくなるおそれがある、という流れ。速さ・大きさ・帰り道は関係ない。
続く文で、端のカモは群れの外側の目を開けていた、真ん中のカモは両目を閉じていた、とある。端だけ違う行動をしていた。両目を閉じていたのは真ん中のカモ。
1日目は脳の半分がより警戒していた、2日目はその差がほぼ消えた。前後が対照的なので However。Therefore（だから）や In addition（さらに）ではつながらない。

sets.passage:
Slow Travel

Many people try to see as many famous places as possible when they go on vacation. They visit three or four cities in a week and spend much of their time on trains and buses. In recent years, however, a different style called "slow travel" has become popular. Instead of rushing from place to place, slow travelers ( 1 ). They might rent an apartment in one small town for two weeks and explore the area slowly.

Supporters say that this way of traveling has several advantages. Because slow travelers often shop at local markets and cook their own meals, they get a better idea of what daily life is like in the area. They also have more chances to talk with local people. ( 2 ), slow travel can be less tiring. Without a busy schedule, people have time to rest, read, or simply sit in a café and watch the world go by.

Slow travel may also be better for the environment. Travelers who stay in one place make fewer trips by plane or car, so they produce less pollution. Some travel companies have noticed this trend and now offer longer stays at lower prices per night. However, slow travel is not for everyone. Many workers can only take a few days off at a time, so they ( 3 ). For them, visiting several places quickly may still be the only way to see the sights they have always dreamed of.

choices: spend a long time in just one place
questions.why: 続く文で「一つの小さな町に2週間アパートを借りる」とある。一か所に長く滞在すること。飛行機だけ・もっと多くの都市・高級ホテルは本文と逆か無関係。
前の文までは利点（地元の生活が分かる・地元の人と話せる）。後ろも「疲れにくい」という別の利点を加えている。追加なので In addition。On the other hand（一方で）は反対の内容が来る時。

choices: prefer to cook their own meals
spend too much money on food
cannot easily travel in this way
questions.why: 直前で「数日しか休めない人が多い」、続く文で「彼らには急いで回るのが唯一の方法」とある。だから長期滞在のスロートラベルは難しい。料理・海外に行かない・食費の話ではない。

sets.passage:
Repair Cafés

When a toaster or a lamp stops working, many people simply throw it away and buy a new one. In some towns, however, people have another choice. Once a month, volunteers open a "repair café" in a community hall or a school. Visitors bring broken items, and the volunteers, many of whom are retired engineers or tailors, ( 1 ). There is no fee, but visitors are asked to put a small donation in a box if they are happy with the result.

The cafés are not only about saving money. The volunteers do not fix things while visitors wait in another room. Instead, they ask the owners to sit beside them and watch each step. In this way, ( 2 ). Many people who once thought that machines were too difficult to understand now repair simple problems at home by themselves. Some even return to the café later as volunteers and help other people with their broken things.

Repair cafés also help to reduce waste. According to one group of organizers, about 60 percent of the items brought to their events can be fixed. That means fewer old machines and clothes end up in the garbage. ( 3 ), not everything can be saved. Some modern products are made so that their parts cannot be opened or replaced, and the volunteers have to tell their owners that nothing can be done. The organizers hope that companies will start making products that are easier to repair.

choices: try to fix them for free
take the items to a factory
questions.why: 続く文で「料金は無い」「結果に満足したら寄付を」とあり、壊れた物を直す場だと分かる。新品を売る・料理教室・工場へ送る話は無い。

choices: visitors learn how to repair things themselves
the volunteers can work more quickly
visitors do not have to pay anything
the café can stay open longer
questions.why: 持ち主が横で手順を見る→直後に「今では家で自分で直す人が多い」とある。直し方を覚える、という結果。作業の速さや営業時間の話ではない。
前は「約60％は直せる」という良い話、後ろは「すべては救えない」という残念な話。だから Unfortunately（残念ながら）。As a result（その結果）や For example（例えば）ではつながらない。

sets.passage:
A Robot in the Strawberry Field

Strawberries are one of the most popular fruits in the world, but they are not easy to grow. The fruit is soft and can be damaged easily, so it has to be picked by hand. On many farms, it is becoming hard to find enough workers to do this job, especially during the busy spring season when the fruit must be picked every few days. Because of this, some farmers have started using robots that ( 1 ).

These robots move slowly along the rows of plants at night. A camera on each robot takes pictures of every strawberry, and a computer decides whether it is ripe by checking its color and size. If it is ready, a soft arm gently cuts the stem and places the fruit in a box. Since the robots can work while people are sleeping, ( 2 ). This means that the strawberries can be sent to stores early in the morning, when they are still fresh.

The robots are still very expensive, however. Most small farms cannot afford to buy one, and the machines sometimes miss strawberries that are hidden under leaves. ( 3 ), farmers still need some workers to check the fields after the robots have finished. Engineers are now trying to make smaller and cheaper models. They hope that these new robots will also be able to pick other soft fruits, such as tomatoes. They say that in ten years, robots may be as common on farms as tractors are today.

choices: can plant new seeds in winter
can pick the fruit without hurting it
can grow fruit without any water
questions.why: 前の文で「柔らかく傷みやすいので手で摘む必要があり、人手が足りない」とある。だから傷つけずに摘めるロボット。種まき・販売・水無しの話ではない。

choices: farmers have to work longer hours
the fruit can be picked during the night
the robots need to rest during the day
questions.why: 人が寝ている間に働ける→直後に「朝早く新鮮なうちに店へ送れる」とある。夜のうちに摘めるということ。農家の労働時間が長くなるのは逆。
前は「葉の下に隠れたイチゴを見逃すことがある」、後ろは「だからロボットの後に人が畑を確かめる必要がある」。原因→結果なので For this reason。In contrast（対照的に）や Instead（代わりに）は合わない。

sets.passage:
The Return of Board Games

Not long ago, many people believed that board games would disappear. As video games and smartphones became more popular, families seemed to spend less time playing games around a table. In recent years, however, board games have ( 1 ). Sales have increased every year in many countries, and thousands of new games are created each year.

One reason is the rise of board game cafés. At these cafés, customers pay a small fee to stay for a few hours and choose from hundreds of games on the shelves. Staff members explain the rules, so customers do not have to read long instruction books. They can also recommend games that suit the size of the group. For people who live in small apartments, ( 2 ). They can try many games before deciding which one to buy, or simply enjoy playing without buying anything at all.

Some people say that the popularity of board games is a reaction to modern life. Many of us spend all day looking at screens for work and school. When we play a board game, we sit face to face, talk, and laugh together. ( 3 ), board games can be good for the brain. Planning several moves ahead and remembering the rules help players to think carefully. Some schools now use board games in math and history classes for this reason, and teachers say that even quiet students join in.

questions.why: 前は「消えると思われていた」、however の後で「売上が毎年増え新作も多い」。つまり再び人気になった。学校で禁止・値上がり・ネット販売のみの話は無い。

choices: the games are too large to play
the rules are difficult to learn
the fees are often very high
questions.why: 続く文で「買う前にたくさん試せる、買わずに楽しめる」とある。狭い部屋に住む人にとってカフェが特に便利。ルールは店員が説明し、料金は少額なので他は逆。
前は「顔を合わせて話し笑える」という良い点、後ろは「脳にも良い」という別の良い点。追加なので In addition。However（しかし）は反対の内容が来る時。

sets.passage:
Trees That Talk

People often think of trees as living alone, each one standing quietly in its own place. However, scientists have discovered that trees in a forest are actually ( 1 ). Under the ground, their roots are joined by a huge network of tiny fungi. These fungi grow around the roots and spread through the soil, linking trees that may be many meters apart. Some scientists have called this network the "wood wide web."

This network allows trees to share food and water. Tall trees that get plenty of sunlight make more sugar than they need. Some of this sugar travels through the fungi to small young trees growing in the shade below. Without this help, many of the young trees might not survive, because they cannot get enough light to make food by themselves. Scientists have also found that ( 2 ). When insects attack one tree, it can send chemical signals through the network, and nearby trees start producing substances that make their leaves taste bad to the insects.

The fungi also get something in return. Since they cannot make their own food, they take some of the sugar that passes through them. ( 3 ), both the trees and the fungi benefit from working together. These discoveries have changed how some people think about forests. Experts now say that when old, large trees are cut down, the young trees around them may lose an important source of support.

questions.why: 続く文で「根が菌の巨大なネットワークでつながり、離れた木同士を結んでいる」とある。つまり互いにつながっている。成長・移動・落葉の話ではない。

choices: trees can warn each other about danger
questions.why: 続く文で「虫に襲われた木が信号を送り、近くの木が葉をまずくする物質を作る」とある。危険を知らせ合うということ。菌が葉をおいしくするのは逆。
前で「木は菌から食べ物の助けを得て、菌は糖を受け取る」とまとめ、後ろで「両方が得をする」と結論づけている。こうして、という意味の In this way。On the other hand（一方で）は対立する内容の時。

parts.title: 大問3A 長文の内容一致選択（Eメール）
parts.desc: 約225語のEメールを読み、内容に合う答えを3問選ぶ
parts.tip: まず差出人・宛先・件名で「誰が誰に何の用か」をつかむ。設問はほぼ段落の順に1問ずつ。正解は本文の語を言い換えていることが多い（hurt → injured など）。
parts.intro: Read the e-mail and choose the best answer to each question.

sets.passage:
From: Nora Bailey <nora.bailey@example.com>
To: Jessica Lane <jlane@example.net>
Date: September 18
Subject: Our class booth at the school festival

Hi Jessica,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our class booth at the school festival next month. At yesterday's meeting, everyone voted, and we decided to sell homemade cookies and lemonade. Mr. Grant said that all the money we make will go toward our class trip in the spring, so we want to sell as much as possible.

I have a favor to ask. Your older brother works at a bakery, right? Could you ask him if he has any tips for baking a large number of cookies at once? We are planning to make about 300, and none of us has ever baked that many before. Also, if the bakery has any extra paper bags, we would be happy to use them.

One more thing. The festival committee told us that every booth must have a sign. Since you are the best artist in our class, I was hoping you could design it. You don't have to make it alone, though. Kenji and Amy said they can help you paint it on Saturday afternoon in the art room. Please let me know if that time is OK for you.

Thanks,
Nora

questions.q: What does Nora say about the money from the booth?
choices: It will be given to a bakery.
It will pay for the festival committee.
It will be used for a class trip.
It will be used to buy art supplies.
questions.why: 第1段落：売上はすべて春の修学旅行に使われる（go toward our class trip）。パン屋・委員会・画材の話ではない。

questions.q: What is one thing Nora asks Jessica to do?
choices: Buy paper bags at a bakery.
Ask her brother for advice about baking.
Get a job at her brother's bakery.
questions.why: 第2段落：パン屋で働く兄に、たくさんのクッキーを一度に焼くコツを聞いてほしい。300個は全員で作る予定で、袋は「余りがあれば」で買う話ではない。

questions.q: What will happen on Saturday afternoon?
choices: The class will hold a meeting to vote.
Some students will work on a sign together.
The festival committee will check the booths.
Jessica will teach an art class.
questions.why: 第3段落：土曜の午後、Kenji と Amy が美術室で看板を描くのを手伝える。Jessica がデザインし、3人で作る。投票は昨日済んでいる。

sets.passage:
From: Westbrook Cooking School <info@westbrookcooking.example.com>
To: Daniel Ross <d.ross@example.org>
Date: February 3
Subject: Changes to your Thursday class

Dear Mr. Ross,

Thank you for joining our eight-week course, "Easy Meals from Around the World." We are writing to tell you about some changes to the course. Unfortunately, Chef Laura Kim, who was going to teach the class, injured her hand last week. Her doctor has told her not to use knives for at least a month.

Because of this, Chef Marco Bell will teach the first four lessons. Chef Bell has run his own restaurant for fifteen years and is especially good at Italian and Spanish cooking. Chef Kim hopes to return for the second half of the course. The lessons will still be held on Thursday evenings from 7:00 to 9:00, but the room has changed. Please go to Kitchen B on the second floor instead of Kitchen A.

We understand that some students signed up because of Chef Kim. If you would like to cancel, we will give you a full refund. You can also move to her Saturday morning course, which will start in April. To choose one of these options, please reply to this e-mail by February 10. If we do not hear from you, we will keep you in the Thursday class.

We look forward to cooking with you.

Westbrook Cooking School

questions.q: What is the problem with Chef Laura Kim?
choices: She cannot use knives for a while because of an injury.
She has decided to open her own restaurant.
She can only teach on Saturday mornings.
She does not know how to cook Italian food.
questions.why: 第1段落：手をけがして、医者に少なくとも1か月は包丁を使わないように言われた。injured her hand を an injury と言い換えている。

questions.q: What will change about the Thursday class?
choices: The place where it is held.
questions.why: 第2段落：木曜夜7時〜9時は変わらないが、部屋が Kitchen A から2階の Kitchen B に変わる。曜日・時間・回数は変わらない。

questions.q: What should Mr. Ross do if he wants to stay in the Thursday class?
choices: Reply to the e-mail by February 10.
He does not need to do anything.
Visit Kitchen A on the second floor.
Pay an extra fee in April.
questions.why: 第3段落：返事が無ければ木曜クラスのままになる。2月10日までの返事が要るのは、返金か土曜クラスへの変更を選ぶ時だけ。

sets.passage:
From: Ryan Cooper <ryan.c@example.com>
To: Ben Walsh <benwalsh@example.net>
Date: April 22
Subject: Fun run in May

Hi Ben,

How are you? I haven't seen you since your birthday party. I'm writing because there's going to be a charity fun run in Riverside Park on May 18. It's only five kilometers, and the money from the entry fees will be used to build a new playground in the park. I've already signed up, and I was wondering if you'd like to join me.

I know you said you haven't run much since you hurt your knee last year. Don't worry, though. This isn't a race, and lots of people walk the whole way. Some people even run in funny costumes! My sister ran it last year dressed as a banana. If you want, we could practice together on Sunday mornings before the event. There's a nice flat path along the river that wouldn't be too hard on your knee.

The entry fee is $20, and every runner gets a T-shirt. If you sign up before the end of April, though, the fee is only $15. You can register on the park's website. After the run, there will be food trucks and live music near the lake, so it should be a fun day even if we're tired. Let me know what you think!

Ryan

questions.q: What will the money from the entry fees be used for?
choices: Building something for children to play on.
Repairing the path along the river.
questions.why: 第1段落：参加費は公園の新しい遊び場（playground）づくりに使われる。それを「子どもが遊ぶ物」と言い換えている。

questions.q: Why does Ryan suggest practicing on Sunday mornings?
choices: To win a prize in the race.
To make costumes with his sister.
To meet people from the park office.
To help Ben get ready without hurting his knee.
questions.why: 第2段落：昨年ひざを痛めた Ben に、ひざに負担の少ない平らな道で一緒に練習しようと提案している。これはレースではないので賞の話は無い。

questions.q: How can Ben pay less to enter the fun run?
choices: By registering before the end of April.
By wearing a costume on the day.
By buying food at the lake.
questions.why: 第3段落：参加費は20ドルだが、4月末までに申し込めば15ドル。仮装や歩くことで安くなるとは書いていない。

sets.passage:
From: Helen Moore <helen.moore@example.com>
To: Yuki Sato <yuki.sato@example.jp>
Date: July 9

parts.title: 大問3B 長文の内容一致選択（説明文）
parts.desc: 約335語の説明文を読み、内容に合う答えを5問選ぶ
parts.tip: 1〜4問目はほぼ段落の順に1問ずつ。最後の「Which of the following statements is true?」は全体から選ぶので、選択肢の数字や「一部」「すべて」を本文と照らし合わせる。
parts.intro: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.

sets.passage:
Songs That Get Stuck

Have you ever heard a song on the radio in the morning and then found it playing again and again in your head all day? This experience is very common. In one survey, about 90 percent of people said that it happened to them at least once a week. Scientists call these songs "earworms," and in recent years, they have started to study why they appear and how people can get rid of them.

Researchers have found that some songs are more likely to become earworms than others. These songs usually have a fast beat and a simple melody that is easy to sing. They also often contain a short part that is repeated many times. Interestingly, people do not need to like a song for it to get stuck in their heads. Many people say that their earworms are songs that they actually find annoying, such as music from television commercials.

Earworms also tend to appear at certain times. They often start when people have just listened to a song several times, or when they are doing an easy task, such as walking or washing the dishes. When the mind does not have much to do, it seems to fill the empty space with music. Feeling stressed or tired can also make earworms more likely.

So what can people do when a song will not leave their heads? One study found that chewing gum can help, because moving the jaw makes it harder for the brain to "sing" silently. Other researchers suggest doing a task that needs attention but is not too difficult, such as a word puzzle. Some people find that listening to the whole song from beginning to end works, too. This may be because the brain feels that the song has finally been completed.

For most people, earworms are only a small problem, and they usually disappear within a few hours. In fact, some scientists believe that they may have a useful side. Repeating sounds in our heads may have helped early humans to remember important information before writing was invented.

questions.q: According to the passage, a survey showed that
choices: only musicians have songs stuck in their heads.
earworms usually last for several weeks.
people stop having earworms as they grow older.
most people have earworms fairly often.
questions.why: 第1段落：約90％の人が少なくとも週1回は経験すると答えた。つまり多くの人がかなりよく経験する。音楽家だけ・数週間続く・年齢の話は無い。

questions.q: What is one feature of songs that often become earworms?
choices: They are songs that people love very much.
They have a slow and difficult melody.
They have a short part that is repeated.
They are always played on the radio.
questions.why: 第2段落：速いビート・簡単なメロディー・何度も繰り返される短い部分。好きな曲である必要はなく、うっとうしい曲も多い、とあるので1つ目は誤り。

questions.q: When are earworms likely to start?
choices: When people are doing something that is not difficult.
When people are concentrating very hard.
When people have not heard any music for a long time.
When people are talking with their friends.
questions.why: 第3段落：歩く・皿洗いなど簡単な作業をしている時に始まりやすい。頭が暇だと音楽で埋めるらしい。集中している時は逆。

questions.q: Why might listening to a whole song help to stop an earworm?
choices: The brain gets tired of the singer's voice.
The listener will learn the words correctly.
The listener will start to dislike the song.
The brain may feel that the song is finished.
questions.why: 第4段落：最初から最後まで聞くと効くのは、脳が「曲がついに終わった」と感じるからかもしれない、とある。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Chewing gum makes earworms last longer.
Earworms usually stay for several days.
Stress makes earworms less likely to appear.
Some scientists think earworms may have helped people in the past.
questions.why: 第5段落：頭の中で音を繰り返すことが、文字の無い時代の人の記憶に役立ったかもしれない、と考える科学者がいる。ガムは止めるのに役立つ、数時間で消える、ストレスで起きやすくなる、なので他は誤り。

sets.passage:
The Boat That Brings Books

In the region around the Varra River, there are dozens of small villages that cannot be reached by road. For many years, people living there had to travel for hours by boat to reach the nearest town. As a result, it was difficult for children to get books, and many of them had never visited a library.

Ana Reyes grew up in one of these villages. As a child, she loved reading, but her family owned only three books, which she read again and again. When she later became a teacher in the town, she often thought about the children she had left behind. In 2012, she bought an old fishing boat with money she had saved for ten years. With help from her two brothers, she painted it yellow, built shelves inside, and filled them with about 500 books that had been given by people in the town.

Every Saturday, the "Book Boat" travels along the river and stops at four villages. When it arrives, children run down to the river to meet it. Reyes reads stories aloud, and children can borrow two books each until the boat returns. At first, some parents did not see the point of reading and wanted their children to help with fishing instead. However, after Reyes started teaching adults to read in the evenings, many parents changed their minds.

Running the boat has not always been easy. During the rainy season, the river becomes dangerous, and the boat sometimes cannot travel for weeks. Also, books can be damaged by the wet air. To solve this problem, Reyes now keeps the books in plastic boxes, and volunteers repair old books every Sunday.

Today, the Book Boat carries more than 2,000 books, and two other teachers have joined the project. Some of the first children who borrowed books from the boat are now in high school, and one of them hopes to study to become a teacher. Reyes says that this is the best reward she could ever receive.

questions.q: Why was it difficult for children in the villages to get books?
choices: Books were too expensive for most teachers.
Their parents did not allow them to go to school.
The town library was closed for many years.
Their villages were far from a town and had no roads.
questions.why: 第1段落：道路で行けない村で、町まで船で何時間もかかった。その結果、本を手に入れにくかった。値段・学校・図書館の閉館の話ではない。

questions.q: How did Ana Reyes get the books for the boat?
choices: She bought them with money she had saved.
Her brothers wrote them for the children.
People in the town gave them to her.
A fishing company sent them to the villages.
questions.why: 第2段落：約500冊は町の人から贈られた（had been given by people in the town）。貯金で買ったのは船。兄弟は棚づくりなどを手伝った。

questions.q: Why did many parents change their minds about reading?
choices: Their children caught more fish than before.
Reyes began to teach adults how to read.
The boat started to bring food as well as books.
Reyes paid the children to read books.
questions.why: 第3段落：最初は読書の意味が分からず漁を手伝わせたい親もいたが、Reyes が夜に大人に読み方を教え始めると、考えを変えた。

questions.q: What problem does the passage mention?
choices: Children often forget to return books.
Books can be harmed by the wet air.
The boat is too small to carry many books.
Volunteers do not have time to help on Sundays.
questions.why: 第4段落：雨季は川が危険になる、湿気で本が傷む、という問題。その対策としてプラスチックの箱と日曜のボランティアによる修理がある。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: The Book Boat stops at a different village every day.
Reyes has stopped teaching in the town.
The Book Boat now carries about 500 books.
One of the children who borrowed books wants to become a teacher.
questions.why: 第5段落：最初に本を借りた子の一人が、先生を目指して勉強したいと思っている。船は毎週土曜に4つの村、本は今2,000冊以上なので他は誤り。

sets.passage:
The Dance of the Honeybees

Honeybees live in large groups called colonies, and some of their members spend the day flying from flower to flower to collect food. A single colony needs a huge amount of food to survive, so it is important for bees to find good flowers quickly. Interestingly, when one bee discovers a rich source of food, it can tell the others exactly where to go. It does this not with sounds but with a special kind of dance.

When the bee returns to the hive, it moves across the wall of the hive in a figure-eight pattern. In the middle of the pattern, it walks in a straight line while shaking its body from side to side. This part is called the "waggle." The direction of the waggle shows the direction of the food. If the bee waggles straight up, the food is in the same direction as the sun. If it waggles to the right, the food is to the right of the sun.

The dance also shows how far away the food is. The longer the waggle lasts, the farther the bees must fly. A waggle of about one second means that the food is roughly one kilometer away. Other bees stay close to the dancer and touch it with their antennae to understand the message. Then they leave the hive and fly straight to the flowers.

Scientists have also found that bees can adjust their dances as the day goes on. Because the sun moves across the sky, the direction of the food compared to the sun keeps changing. Amazingly, bees seem to know this and change the angle of their waggle without being taught.

Today, researchers study bee dances to learn more about the environment. By recording dances in city hives, they can find out where bees are collecting food and which areas have enough flowers. This information can help cities decide where to plant more flowers to support bees and other insects.

questions.q: Why is it important for bees to find good flowers quickly?
choices: A colony needs a very large amount of food.
Flowers only open for a few minutes each day.
Other insects may take over the hive.
Bees can only fly for a short time.
questions.why: 第1段落：一つのコロニーが生き延びるには大量の食べ物が要るので、良い花を早く見つけることが大切。花の時間・他の虫・飛べる時間の話は無い。

questions.q: What does the direction of the waggle show?
choices: How many bees should leave the hive.
Where the food is compared to the sun.
What kind of flower the bee has found.
How long the bee has been away.
questions.why: 第2段落：waggle の向きは食べ物の方向を表す。真上なら太陽と同じ方向、右なら太陽の右側。

questions.q: If a bee's waggle lasts for a long time,
choices: the food is far away from the hive.
the food is very close to the hive.
the bee is too tired to fly again.
the other bees will not leave the hive.
questions.why: 第3段落：waggle が長いほど遠くまで飛ばなければならない。約1秒でおよそ1km。

questions.q: What have scientists found about bee dances?
choices: Bees stop dancing in the afternoon.
Young bees must be taught by older bees.
Bees change their dances as the sun moves.
Bees dance differently in each country.
questions.why: 第4段落：太陽が動くと食べ物との角度が変わるので、ハチは教わらなくても waggle の角度を変える。教わる必要があるわけではない。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Bees tell each other about food by making sounds.
Studying bee dances can help cities plan where to grow flowers.
Other bees watch the dance from far away.
City hives have been closed because of the dances.
questions.why: 第5段落：都市の巣のダンスを記録すれば、どこに花を植えるべきか決める手助けになる。ハチは音ではなくダンスで伝え、他のハチは近くで触角を使って理解する。

sets.passage:
Building with Bamboo

When people think of strong building materials, they usually think of steel or concrete. However, in many parts of Asia and South America, people have used bamboo to build houses and bridges for hundreds of years. Recently, architects in other parts of the world have also become interested in this plant.

One reason for this interest is that bamboo grows extremely fast. Some types can grow almost one meter in a single day, and most can be cut and used for building after just three to five years. Trees used for wood, on the other hand, often need 30 years or more. Moreover, bamboo grows back from its roots after it is cut, so new plants do not need to be planted. For these reasons, many people believe it is a better choice for the environment.

Bamboo is also surprisingly strong for its weight. Because it is light, it is easy to carry and can be put together without large machines. In some cities, workers even use bamboo poles instead of metal ones when they repair the outside of tall buildings. Bamboo can also bend without breaking, so houses made of it are less likely to fall down in strong winds.

However, bamboo has some disadvantages. Insects love to eat it, and it can rot quickly if it stays wet. To make it last longer, it must be dried and treated with special chemicals, which adds to the cost. In addition, every piece of bamboo has a slightly different shape and thickness. This makes it hard to use in modern buildings, where materials usually need to be exactly the same size.

To solve this problem, some companies have begun cutting bamboo into thin strips and pressing them together to make flat boards. These boards look like wood and can be used for floors, furniture, and walls. Although bamboo will probably not replace steel and concrete, many experts think that it will play a larger role in building in the future.

questions.q: What does the passage say about bamboo in the first paragraph?
choices: It is stronger than steel and concrete.
It was first used to build houses in Europe.
It has been used for building in some places for a long time.
Architects have stopped using it recently.
questions.why: 第1段落：アジアや南米では何百年も家や橋に使われてきた。鋼やコンクリートより強いとは書いていない。

questions.q: Why do many people think bamboo is good for the environment?
choices: It does not need any water to grow.
It grows quickly and does not need to be planted again.
It can be cut down after only one year.
It is usually grown in large cities.
questions.why: 第2段落：成長が非常に速く（3〜5年で使える）、切っても根から再び生えるので植え直さなくてよい。1年で使えるとは言っていない。

questions.q: What is one advantage of bamboo being light?
choices: It does not bend in strong winds.
It is never eaten by insects.
It can be used without large machines.
It costs less to treat with chemicals.
questions.why: 第3段落：軽いので運びやすく、大きな機械なしで組み立てられる。強風で倒れにくいのは「曲がっても折れない」から。

questions.q: Why is bamboo hard to use in modern buildings?
choices: Each piece is a little different in size.
It is too heavy to carry to high places.
It must be cut into very large boards.
Modern buildings need materials that rot easily.
questions.why: 第4段落：竹は1本ずつ形と太さが少しずつ違い、同じ大きさの材料が必要な現代の建物では使いにくい。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Some companies make flat boards by pressing strips of bamboo together.
Bamboo will soon replace steel in most buildings.
Bamboo lasts longer if it is kept wet.
Trees for wood grow faster than bamboo.

sets.passage:
Clever Crows

Many people think of crows as noisy birds that make a mess of garbage bags. However, scientists who study animal intelligence see them very differently. Crows have large brains for their body size, and in many tests, they have solved problems as well as young children. Some researchers even say that crows are among the smartest animals on Earth.

One skill that surprised scientists is the way some crows use tools. On a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean, crows break off small sticks and shape them into hooks. They then use these hooks to pull insects out of holes in trees. Young crows are not very good at this at first. They watch older birds carefully and practice for many months before they can make good tools of their own.

Crows also have excellent memories. In one study, researchers wore masks while they caught a few crows, measured them, and then let them go. For years afterward, whenever a person wore the same mask near the area, the crows made loud warning calls and flew around the person. What surprised the researchers most was that many of the crows had never been caught themselves. They seemed to have learned about the "dangerous" face from other crows.

In some cities, crows have learned to use human inventions. For example, people have seen crows dropping hard nuts onto roads so that passing cars will crack them open. Some birds even wait at crosswalks and pick up the pieces only when the traffic light turns red and the cars stop.

Not everyone is happy about the birds' intelligence. Because crows learn quickly, it is hard to keep them away from farms and garbage areas. Scarecrows and loud noises usually work for only a short time before the crows realize that there is no real danger. Some cities are now trying new ideas, such as nets that make it difficult for crows to reach food waste.

questions.q: What do some researchers say about crows?
choices: They are one of the most intelligent kinds of animals.
They are smarter than most adult humans.
Their brains are smaller than those of other birds.
They are the noisiest birds in the world.
questions.why: 第1段落：カラスは地球上で最も賢い動物の一つだ、と言う研究者もいる。子どもと同じくらい問題を解けるとあるが、大人より賢いとは書いていない。

questions.q: How do young crows on the islands learn to make tools?
choices: By copying the way humans use sticks.
By watching older crows and practicing.
By being taught in tests by scientists.
By pulling insects out of holes in the ground.
questions.why: 第2段落：若いカラスは最初は下手で、年上の鳥をよく見て何か月も練習する。人間をまねるとは書いていない。虫を引き出すのは木の穴から。

questions.q: What surprised the researchers who wore masks?
choices: The crows forgot the masks after a few days.
Crows that had not been caught also reacted to the masks.
The crows were not afraid of the researchers.
The crows tried to take the masks away.
questions.why: 第3段落：捕まえられたことの無いカラスまで、同じ仮面の人に警告の声を上げた。他のカラスから学んだらしい。何年も覚えていたので「数日で忘れた」は逆。

choices: To collect pieces of nuts safely.
To find garbage that people have dropped.
To cross the road with people.
To make cars stop for them.
questions.why: 第4段落：車にナッツを割らせ、信号が赤になり車が止まった時だけ破片を拾う。車を止めさせているのではなく、止まるのを待っている。

choices: Scarecrows often stop working after a while.

sets.passage:
Farms Inside Buildings

Most of the vegetables we eat are grown in large fields. However, a growing number of companies are now growing food in a completely different way. They use tall buildings, such as old factories and warehouses, and grow plants on shelves that are stacked one on top of another, sometimes ten levels high. This method is called "vertical farming."

In a vertical farm, the plants never see the sun. Instead, they are grown under special LED lights that give them exactly the kind of light they need. The plants also do not grow in soil. Their roots hang in water that contains all the nutrients they need, and computers control the temperature and the amount of water. As a result, crops such as lettuce and herbs can be harvested up to ten times a year, while farmers in fields may get only two or three harvests.

Vertical farms have other advantages, too. Because the plants are grown indoors, there are no insects to damage them, so farmers do not need to use chemicals to protect them. Bad weather, such as heavy rain or a long period without rain, is also not a problem. In addition, many vertical farms are built in or near large cities. The vegetables can be delivered to supermarkets within a few hours of being picked, so they stay fresh and less fuel is used for transportation.

However, vertical farming also has some serious problems. The LED lights and computers need a large amount of electricity, which makes the vegetables expensive to produce. For this reason, most vertical farms grow only light, fast-growing plants. Crops like rice, wheat, and potatoes need too much space and light, so it is still much cheaper to grow them in fields.

Some experts believe that vertical farms will become more common as the cost of electricity from solar and wind power goes down. Others think that they will remain a small part of farming. Either way, they may become an important source of fresh food for people living in crowded cities.

questions.q: What is one feature of vertical farming?
choices: Plants are grown only on the roofs of buildings.
Plants are grown on shelves placed on top of each other.
Farmers use old factories to make farming machines.
Vegetables are grown in fields next to tall buildings.
questions.why: 第1段落：高い建物の中で、何段も重ねた棚で植物を育てる。屋上だけ・機械作り・畑の話ではない。

questions.q: Why can lettuce be harvested many times a year in a vertical farm?
choices: The plants receive more sunlight than in fields.
The soil in the buildings is very rich.
Farmers work longer hours than in fields.
The conditions for growing are carefully controlled.
questions.why: 第2段落：専用のLEDと栄養入りの水を使い、温度や水の量をコンピューターが管理する。その結果、年に最大10回収穫できる。日光や土は使わない。

questions.q: Why are vegetables from vertical farms often fresh?
choices: They are kept in the buildings for a long time.
They are picked only when the weather is good.
They are grown close to where they are sold.
questions.why: 第3段落：多くは大都市の中や近くにあり、摘んで数時間でスーパーへ届く。農薬は不要と書かれているので1つ目は逆。

questions.q: What is one problem with vertical farms?
choices: They cannot grow herbs or lettuce.
They cost a lot to run because of the energy they use.
They need more water than farms in fields.
questions.why: 第4段落：LEDとコンピューターが大量の電気を使い、生産費が高い。屋内なので虫の害は無く、レタスやハーブは主な作物。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Vertical farms are usually built far from cities.
All experts agree that vertical farms will replace fields.
Vertical farms can only harvest crops two or three times a year.
Rice is still cheaper to grow in fields than indoors.
questions.why: 第4段落：米・小麦・じゃがいもは場所と光が多く必要で、畑のほうがずっと安い。都市の近くにあり、専門家の意見は分かれ、収穫は最大年10回なので他は誤り。

sets.passage:
Why Do We Yawn?

Everyone yawns. We yawn when we are tired, when we are bored, and sometimes for no clear reason at all. Babies start yawning even before they are born, and many animals, including dogs, cats, and fish, yawn as well. Although yawning is so common, scientists still do not fully understand why we do it.

For many years, people believed that we yawn because our bodies need more oxygen. According to this idea, taking a deep breath while yawning brings extra oxygen into the blood and helps us stay awake. However, when researchers tested this idea, they found that people did not yawn more when they breathed air that had less oxygen in it. They also did not yawn less when they were given extra oxygen. Most scientists now think that this explanation is wrong.

A newer idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. Like a computer, the brain works best when it is not too hot. When we yawn, we open our mouths wide and take in a large amount of air, which may cool the blood flowing to the head. Supporting this idea, one study found that people yawned more often in warm weather than in very hot weather, when the outside air is too warm to cool anything.

Yawning is also famous for being "catching." Just seeing or hearing someone yawn, or even reading about yawning, can make people start yawning themselves. Interestingly, studies show that we are more likely to catch a yawn from family members and close friends than from strangers. Some researchers believe this shows that catching yawns is connected to our ability to understand other people's feelings.

Young children under the age of about four rarely catch yawns from others. This seems to match the age when children begin to understand that other people have their own thoughts and feelings. So the next time you yawn after seeing a friend do it, it may simply be a sign that you care about that person.

questions.q: What does the passage say about yawning in the first paragraph?
choices: Only humans yawn when they are bored.
Even animals and unborn babies do it.
Scientists have found the exact reason for it.
People yawn only when they are tired.
questions.why: 第1段落：生まれる前の赤ちゃんや犬・猫・魚もあくびをする。理由はまだはっきり分かっておらず、理由が無い時もあくびをする。

questions.q: What did researchers find when they tested the oxygen idea?
choices: People yawned more when they had extra oxygen.
Yawning brought a lot of oxygen into the blood.
People with less oxygen fell asleep quickly.
The amount of oxygen did not change how often people yawned.
questions.why: 第2段落：酸素の少ない空気でもあくびは増えず、酸素を足しても減らなかった。だから酸素説は誤りと考えられている。

questions.q: Why did people yawn less in very hot weather?
choices: The air was too warm to cool down the brain.
They were too tired to open their mouths.
Their brains were already cool enough.
They drank more cold water than usual.
questions.why: 第3段落：とても暑い日は外の空気が熱すぎて何も冷やせないので、あくびが少なかった。これが「脳を冷やす」説の裏付けになっている。

questions.q: People are more likely to catch a yawn from
choices: people who are much older than them.
people who are reading a book.
people who are close to them.
questions.why: 第4段落：知らない人より家族や親しい友人からうつりやすい。他人の気持ちを理解する力とつながっていると考える研究者もいる。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Most scientists still believe the oxygen idea.
Reading about yawning cannot make people yawn.
Very young children seldom catch yawns from other people.
Children start catching yawns before they are born.
questions.why: 第5段落：4歳くらいまでの子どもはほとんど人のあくびがうつらない（rarely → seldom）。酸素説は誤りとされ、読むだけでもうつるので他は誤り。

sets.passage:
A Hotel Made of Ice

In the far north of a cold northern country, there is a small village that becomes famous every winter. When the temperature drops below minus 20 degrees, workers begin to build a hotel made completely of ice and snow. The hotel has about 30 rooms, a restaurant, and even a small concert hall. Every spring, when the weather gets warmer, the whole building melts and flows back into the nearby river.

The ice used for the hotel comes from that same river. Each March, when the river ice is thick and clear, workers cut out huge blocks, some weighing more than two tons. The blocks are kept in a large cold storage building through the summer. Then, in November, the workers take them out and start building. It takes about six weeks to finish the hotel, and around 50 people, including builders, artists, and designers, work on it.

What makes the hotel special is that it is different every year. Each autumn, artists from around the world send in designs for the rooms. A group of judges chooses about a dozen of them, and the artists come to the village to carve their rooms by hand. One year, a room was made to look like the inside of a whale. Another room had a bed shaped like a giant flower. Because of this, many guests come back again and again to see the new designs.

Staying in the hotel is an unusual experience. The temperature inside the rooms is always around minus 5 degrees. Guests sleep in thick sleeping bags on beds covered with animal skins. Most people stay for only one night in the ice rooms and spend the rest of their trip in warm cabins nearby. The hotel also offers activities such as dog sledding and ice carving lessons.

The hotel has brought many changes to the village. Before it opened, few tourists visited in winter, and many young people moved away to find work. Today, the hotel employs more than 100 local people during the busy season, and new restaurants and shops have opened.

questions.q: What happens to the hotel every spring?
choices: It is moved to a different village.
It melts and becomes water again.
It is made bigger for summer visitors.
questions.why: 第1段落：春に暖かくなると建物全体が溶けて近くの川に戻る。移動・修理・夏の拡張の話は無い。

questions.q: Why do workers cut ice from the river in March?
choices: The river is warmest at that time.
Artists send in their designs in March.
The ice is thick and clear at that time.
The hotel must be finished by April.
questions.why: 第2段落：3月は川の氷が厚く透明なので、その時に大きなブロックを切り出す。デザインが送られるのは秋、建設は11月から。

questions.q: Why do many guests visit the hotel more than once?
choices: The rooms are designed in a new way each year.
They can stay there for free the second time.
They want to take ice carving lessons again.
The hotel is warmer than other hotels.
questions.why: 第3段落：毎年世界の芸術家のデザインで部屋が作り直されるので、新しいデザインを見に何度も来る。

questions.q: What do most guests do during their stay?
choices: Sleep in the ice rooms for a whole week.
Build their own rooms out of snow.
Spend one night in the ice hotel and the other nights somewhere warmer.
Stay in cabins without visiting the ice rooms.
questions.why: 第4段落：ほとんどの人は氷の部屋に1泊だけし、残りは近くの暖かいコテージで過ごす。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Only artists from the village design the rooms.
The hotel has created many jobs for people in the village.
The temperature inside the rooms is above zero.
More young people left the village after the hotel opened.
questions.why: 第5段落：繁忙期に地元の100人以上を雇い、新しい店もできた。芸術家は世界中から、室温は約マイナス5度、若者が出て行ったのは開業前なので他は誤り。

Online grocery shopping has some advantages. People do not have to carry heavy bags of rice or bottles of water home from the store. Also, it is easy to compare prices on a screen, which can help people save money.

However, there are some disadvantages. Customers cannot check the freshness of fruit and vegetables before buying them. In addition, many services charge a delivery fee, especially when the order is small.

Some public libraries have started lending more than books. People can borrow items such as tools, camping tents, and musical instruments, just as they borrow books.

These "libraries of things" have some good points. People can use an item that they need only once or twice without buying it, so they can save money. Also, sharing items means that fewer new products need to be made.

However, there are also some problems. Borrowed items are sometimes returned broken or dirty, and libraries must pay to repair or clean them. In addition, popular items, such as tents in summer, are often not available when people want them.

Using robots has several advantages. Robots can work for many hours without getting tired, so businesses can solve the problem of not having enough workers. Also, some guests enjoy seeing the robots and take pictures of them.

On the other hand, robots have some limits. They cannot answer unusual questions from customers or deal with sudden problems. In addition, buying and repairing robots can cost a lot of money, especially for small businesses.

parts.title: リスニング第1部 会話の内容一致選択
parts.desc: 2人の会話（2往復ほど）を聞き、質問の答えを4つから選ぶ。放送は1回
parts.tip: 放送の前に選択肢を見て、主語と動詞から質問を予想する。会話の後半で「でも～」「それなら～」と予定が変わることが多いので、最後の発言まで聞く。
parts.intro: Listen to the conversation and the question. Choose the best answer.

sets.script:
W: Dad, can you drive me to the library this afternoon? I need to return some books.
M: Sorry, Amy. I have to take the car to the repair shop at two.
W: Oh. Then I'll ride my bike. Could you check the tires for me first?
M: Sure. I'll do it right after lunch.
Question: What will the man do after lunch?

questions.q: What will the man do after lunch?
choices: Drive his daughter to the library.
Buy new tires for the car.
questions.why: 娘に自転車のタイヤを見てと頼まれ、昼食のすぐ後にやると答えている。図書館へ送るのは車の修理があるので断った。

sets.script:

W: It's ready now. I'll also bring you a free coffee for waiting.
Question: What will the woman give the man?

questions.q: What will the woman give the man?
choices: A discount on his next meal.
questions.why: 待たせたおわびに無料のコーヒー（a free coffee）を持ってくる、と言っている。at no cost＝無料で。

They seemed to be enjoying themselves.

They can fly for short distances.
They swim slowly to save energy.

By teaching Japanese at a school.

To win a prize in a contest.
To have good luck in the new year.

Safer Cycling

Many people ride bicycles to work or school. Some cities have built special lanes that only bicycles can use. Riders use these lanes instead of busy roads, and by doing so they can travel more safely. Such lanes are also encouraging more people to start riding bicycles in their daily lives.

tasks.prompt: According to the passage, how can riders travel more safely?
tasks.ja: 答えの形：By using special lanes (only for bicycles) instead of busy roads.（by doing so / in this way の前を見る）
